items.headline: Anthropic opens Milan + Seoul offices; Project Glasswing update lands 10,000+ critical findings
items.diff_narrative: Friday's top-of-mix Anthropic storyline was the Series H $65 billion close at a $965 billion post-money valuation paired with same-day Claude Opus 4.8 GA and the Dynamic Workflows research preview — a corporate-finance plus flagship-model-ship bundle distributed across Claude API, Amazon Bedrock, Google Vertex AI, GitHub Copilot, and Microsoft 365 Copilot. Saturday opens a structurally distinct Anthropic storyline focused on geographic footprint and AI-found vulnerability disclosure rather than financing or model GA. Inside the same 48-hour window either side of the Thursday Series H close, Anthropic appointed KiYoung Choi (ex-Snowflake Korea Country Manager) as Representative Director of Korea on Tuesday May 26 and opened a Milan office on Wednesday May 27 — its sixth European footprint after London, Dublin, Paris, Zurich, and Munich — under GDPR-compliant data residency. Bridging both is a Project Glasswing update credited to Claude Mythos Preview for 10,000+ high- or critical-severity findings across roughly 50 partners (Mozilla closed 271 Firefox vulnerabilities at 10x prior rate; Cloudflare surfaced 2,000 bugs with 400 rated high or critical), 530 high/critical disclosures to maintainers and 75 patches completed, plus a wolfSSL CVE-2026-5194 certificate-forgery flaw (CVSS 9.1) on a TLS library embedded in roughly five billion IoT, automotive, and industrial-control devices.

items.headline: SpaceX S-1 vs Musk: $37.5B disclosure gap on the Anthropic Colossus 1 compute deal
items.diff_narrative: Friday's regulator-and-disclosure thread was upstream at the frontier-lab tier: OpenAI's Frontier Governance Framework mapping its Preparedness Framework onto California SB 53 and the EU AI Act Code of Practice, with systemic risk explicitly anchored to greater-than-50-fatality or $1-billion-property-damage incident thresholds. Saturday opens a structurally different disclosure storyline at the IPO-prospectus tier: the language in SpaceX's May 20 S-1 collides publicly with Elon Musk's own X-post characterization of the Anthropic Memphis Colossus 1 compute arrangement, leaving roughly a $37.5 billion gap between the two on the day SpaceX confirms its institutional roadshow opens Monday June 8 at a $1.75T-$2T target range and ~$75B raise. The S-1 describes Anthropic as agreeing to pay a $1.25 billion monthly fee through May 2029 — implying a ~$45 billion three-year commitment — while Musk said on X the arrangement is a 180-day lease with 90-day mutual cancellation, putting the maximum obligation at ~$7.5 billion and adding that SpaceX may reclaim the capacity for xAI if compute gets super tight. The underlying asset is the 220,000+ NVIDIA GPU, 300+ MW Memphis cluster originally built to train Grok; SPCX is confirmed on Nasdaq with pricing scheduled June 11 and first trade June 12.

items.headline: Figure AI BotQ hits 1 humanoid/hour on F.03; 350+ shipped, 55 this week
items.diff_narrative: Friday's vendor-tape storyline was Cerebras Systems (NASDAQ:CBRS) closing the week at $242.59 inside a $241.53-$268.78 intraday range with Russell 1000 small-to-large-cap migration and S&P Dow Jones fast-track inclusion crystallizing into the weekly print — a public-markets index-reconstitution catalyst. Saturday opens a structurally different vendor disclosure storyline on the humanoid-robotics throughput axis. Figure AI on Wednesday May 27 disclosed that its BotQ manufacturing facility scaled Figure 03 production from one robot per day to one robot per hour over the prior 120 days — a 24x throughput improvement — pushing total shipments past 350 units across more than 10 product variants, with 55 robots planned for the week and over 9,000 actuators produced. The ramp leans on dedicated assembly lines distributed across 150+ workstations, custom manufacturing software, and tightened supplier quality controls that pushed first-pass yields above 80%. This pulls Figure into the same fixed-cohort-on-the-factory-floor frame Apptronik's Apollo Gen 2 sits in (10-unit Mercedes-Benz Tuscaloosa cohort cleared 120h zero-MTBF preflight earlier in the week), and humanoid pure-play comps now have two named OEM-anchored counts shipping inside a 14-day window on top of Tesla Optimus Gen 3's summer-2026 Fremont production-start target.

items.headline: Bay Area June-July calendar: Snowflake Summit, Microsoft Build, WWDC, Databricks Summit, AI Engineer World's Fair
items.diff_narrative: Friday's forward-events digest locked the Bay Area June lineup around three Moscone-scale anchors — Snowflake Summit 26 (June 1-4), Databricks Data + AI Summit (June 15-18), and AI Engineer World's Fair (June 29-July 2) — with ACM CAIS 2026 still active as the spring agentic-systems cycle wrap and AI Tinkerers SF VIP Dinner as the smaller community signal. Saturday carries the same calendar forward and extends it with two structurally important vendor anchors that fit in the same five-week window: Microsoft Build 2026 runs Tuesday-Wednesday June 2-3 at Fort Mason Center San Francisco with the Windows Agent Framework slated for open-source MIT-licensed release on day one, plus Copilot Agent Mode and a Windows Agent Store marketplace; Apple WWDC26 runs Monday-Friday June 8-12 with the keynote Monday at 10:00 AM PT and an Apple Park in-person event on day one open to registered developers via random lottery. The far-end of the calendar now surfaces GitHub Universe (San Francisco Fort Mason, October 28-29, registration open with standard pricing kicking in early September) and AWS re:Invent (Las Vegas, November 30-December 4, registration opening June 16 with early-bird savings through August 25). The ACM CAIS 2026 closing keynote that capped Friday's window has rolled off — its 3:30 PM Friday slot was the date-passed boundary and is no longer in scope for forward-looking attendable events.
